source.title: SELMA: Learning and Merging Skill-Specific Text-to-Image Experts with Auto-Generated Data
source.authors: Jialu Li; Jaemin Cho; Yi-Lin Sung; Jaehong Yoon; Mohit Bansal

record.file_problem: The full paper is present; some figure text is garbled, but the relevant tables and prose are readable.
record.tranche_reason: Extends weak-to-strong generalization to text-to-image diffusion models, using images generated by a weaker model as training data for a stronger one. It does not use the original PGR measure or the original language-model setup.
record.gate_note: Table 3 directly reports the stronger model fine-tuned on images from the weaker model and compares it with the weaker-model baseline. The paper does not calculate PGR or provide a strong-model ceiling trained on true labels. Other SELMA results using same-model-generated data do not test weak-to-strong generalization.
record.test_reason: Sec. 5.4 and Table 3 fine-tune SDXL on images generated by the weaker SD v2 and compare it with SD v2 and SDXL. The authors frame this as weak-to-strong generalization in text-to-image diffusion models. It is a new setting (generative vision) with no PGR and no ground-truth-trained strong ceiling.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Authors conclude fine-tuning SDXL on SD v2-generated images improves faithfulness and human-preference scores over SDXL, competitive with self-generated data, suggesting 'promising' weak-to-strong generalization in T2I models.
record.recipe_differences: This is a text-to-image extension: the weaker model generates training images paired with prompts, and SDXL is fine-tuned with LoRA. The paper does not use the original language-model label-supervision setup or report PGR.
record.method_sensitivity: The training image generator changes the reported outcomes: SDXL trained on SD v2-generated images scores 81.3 on DSG versus 80.2 when trained on SDXL-generated images; the latter scores higher on TIFA and the three human-preference metrics.
record.problems: The weak-to-strong comparison uses one weak/strong model pair. No PGR, true-label-trained strong-model ceiling, or uncertainty estimates are reported. Outcomes also vary by metric; PickScore for the weak-generator condition is below the SDXL base score.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant weak-to-strong Table 3 results were omitted. Results using same-model-generated data or other SELMA training methods were not included because they do not test the weaker-supervisor condition.

untested.parts: PGR, and any strong-model ceiling trained on ground-truth data. Only one weak/strong pair (SD v2 → SDXL).
No training change is evaluated for its effect on weak-to-strong gains.
No variation of supervisor or student size, task, or predictors.
No tests of distribution shift, error similarity, or exploitation.
Only text-to-image generation is tested. Vision classification, the setting of the original, is not tested.

record.verdict_notes: The setup differs from the original: the 'supervision' is images generated by the weak model from LLM-written skill prompts. Gains may come mostly from the targeted prompts; SD v2 self-training also gives +7.4 DSG. Table 3 row 5 (SDXL trained on its own images: 80.2/85.6/22.0/1.09/29.9) is the closest proxy for an upper reference but is not a ground-truth ceiling. Rows_left_out declares it as excluded. A single checkpoint was selected on DSG, which may favour the DSG result (r1). No uncertainty is reported.

versions.untested_parts: The study reports the stronger model's performance against the weak-model baseline, but does not calculate PGR or compare against a strong model trained on true labels.
No training change is evaluated for its effect on PGR.
Only one weak/strong model pair and one task family are used; supervisor/student size, task, and representation predictors are not systematically varied.
The study does not test distribution shift, supervisor/student error similarity, or student exploitation of supervisor blind spots.
No theoretical conditions for student superiority are tested or argued.
The study tests text-to-image diffusion models, not other non-language modalities.

rows.operation_detail: Fine-tune SDXL using SELMA image-text data whose images were generated by SD v2

rows.check: Correct values (81.3 vs SD v2 70.3, SDXL base 73.3). Untrained SDXL already beats the weak supervisor, so beating the weak model alone is uninformative. The +8.0 over SDXL base is the informative gain.
